Mikhail and I collaborated briefly on a server scalability project at NexaGame Studios. Our interactions centered around aligning infrastructure needs with game development timelines. His approach to problem-solving felt pragmatic—always focused on immediate reliability without over-engineering.  

Daily, he prioritized proactive monitoring and quick triage. During a recent launch, he identified a potential database bottleneck hours before it could disrupt player sessions. While AWS tools were already in use, his insistence on automating routine checks freed the team to focus on creative tasks. Chaos engineering became a regular practice under his guidance, with small, targeted stress tests that prevented major outages.  

One standout moment was when he reconfigured a redundant system during a holiday event, ensuring zero downtime for thousands of concurrent users. His calm under pressure and ability to distill complex issues into clear actions stood out. He also mentored junior engineers, sharing tricks for debugging without overcomplicating solutions.  

Mikhail’s strength lies in his balance of technical rigor and teamwork. He doesn’t just solve problems—he ensures others can too. His work ethic is reliable, and his focus on stability makes him a steady presence in high-stakes environments. I’d recommend him for roles where reliability and collaboration are key.
